targets.title: Flight to Safety: COVID-Induced Changes in the Intensity of Status Quo Preference and Voting Behavior.
targets.evidence_quote: We first reproduce Bisbee and Honig (2022)’s findings, figures, and tables using the code provided via the Harvard Dataverse.3 We find that all code clearly reproduces the paper’s results.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: We find that all code clearly reproduces the paper’s results.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Using the updated method, we find that though the effect of Covid continues to have a negative effect, the results are no longer statistically significant. That said, this method suffers from a low number of DMAs, with the small N resulting from our aggregation likely driving this result.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original-data reanalysis reproduced the numbers, but the alternative DiD specification removed statistical significance. Authors describe mixed results and qualify that test because of small N, while finding House results largely robust. Expanded candidate coverage concerns the same original election data rather than a fresh independent sample.

reasoning: Re-runs original code and tests alternative specifications of original election data; supplementary expansion corrects and extends original candidate coverage.
